topic: Mohe 1997 eclipse gravity anomaly — Unnikrishnan reframe (EXP-608) adversarial verification
change_summary: EXP-608 reframed the Unnikrishnan et al. 2001 citation from the factually-wrong ‘cites a counter-paper against itself’ to a selective-citation/over-claim argument, and reduced ‘silently’ from 7 occurrences to 2. Verdict unchanged (Not Demonstrated).
our_argument_summary: WIN-011 holds the gravity claim Not Demonstrated: the dome relocated the anomaly from -6.5 uGal at eclipse maximum (where its own sources report null) to ~7.0 +/- 2.7 uGal at first/last contact (where Wang 2000 had already put it) without flagging the change in its commit message; the dome’s own kappa=1.67 coupling fails its own 5% tolerance on the rewritten 7.0 value; superconducting-gravimeter records already came back null; and the dome’s headline Unnikrishnan 2001 citation, deployed offensively against the rival globe shielding hypothesis, is selective because the same paper rules out the 1997 data as evidence for any new gravitational property.

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: Standard physics (Yang & Wang 2002 DOI 10.1023/A:1021119023985; Van Flandern & Yang 2003 DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.67.022002) explains the contact-phase valleys as thermal-tilt / atmospheric instrument artifacts — i.e. NOT a real gravity signal. The dome is not renaming a standard mechanism; it asserts a real anomalous coupling that standard physics treats as instrumental. False holds.

The dome’s contact-phase ‘timing rule’ was announced in the 2026-04-17 rewrite for 26-year-old data — adoption of a known measurement labeled a prediction. True holds.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The ~7.0 uGal magnitude is adopted from Wang et al.; kappa=1.67 is a fitted ratio of two observational constants, not traced from disc_radius/firmament_height. No derivation from dome geometry to this value. False holds.

holes_found.description: The reframed Unnikrishnan argument slightly over-reads the paper’s quantitative scope, creating a symmetry exposure on a page whose whole thesis is that the dome over-stretches its sources. Unnikrishnan, Mohapatra & Gillies (2001, PRD 63 062002) quantitatively bound gravitational SHIELDING — they constrain the Majorana extinction / shielding coefficient using Wang’s before/after-eclipse data (confirmed via search 2026-06-09: ‘constrain the characteristic shielding parameter to the lowest bound ever from a terrestrial experiment’). Their abstract’s broader phrase ‘or could be pointing to some new property of gravitation’ is the framing question they answer by showing the 1997 data do not support an anomalous signal at all. Our detail_evidence says the paper ‘rules out the dome’s own mechanism in the same breath’ and detail_verdict_text says it ‘rules out the 1997 data as evidence of any new gravitational property — the dome’s own electromagnetic coupling included.’ A confirmed-reader dome defender can retort: Unnikrishnan parameterized mass-shielding, not an electromagnetic-gravitational coupling, so its numerical bound does not specifically exclude the ECM mechanism — and we would be doing precisely the source-stretching we accuse the dome of.
holes_found.recommendation: Tighten to the data-as-evidence framing, which is bulletproof and already present in the last clause (‘treats the contact-phase valleys as conventional rather than evidence of new gravity at all’). Replace ‘rules out the dome’s own mechanism’ with ‘rules out the 1997 data as evidence FOR the dome’s mechanism’: the paper reads the same contact-phase valleys the dome relies on as conventional/instrumental, so the dataset the dome cites cannot simultaneously be authoritative against the globe and evidence of new gravity for the dome. That keeps the (strong, correct) point and drops the over-claim.

holes_found.description: kappa-error arithmetic is loosely anchored. detail_evidence/detail_verdict_text state a ‘7.25% error against 1.67’ for the rewritten 7.0 uGal: 10.9/7.0 = 1.557, and |1.557-1.67| is 7.26% of 1.557 but 6.77% of 1.67. The 7.25% figure is measured against the recomputed 1.557, not against the stated comparator 1.67. Both exceed the dome’s 5% tolerance so the conclusion is unaffected; this is pre-existing and outside EXP-608’s direct edit, hence minor.
holes_found.recommendation: Either say ‘6.8% against 1.67’ or ‘7.25% relative to the recomputed kappa of 1.557’ so the percentage and its denominator agree. Low priority.

stronger_arguments.description: Lead the Unnikrishnan paragraph with the bulletproof reading rather than the over-claim: the dome cannot treat Unnikrishnan as authoritative on the 1997 Mohe dataset to kill the globe’s shielding hypothesis while exempting the SAME dataset from the same paper’s reading of the contact-phase valleys as conventional. The leverage is the shared dataset and the shared instrumental reading, not a claim that the paper parameterized the ECM coupling.

kernel_of_truth.description: The reframe is a genuine, well-executed improvement and the analyst found the right kernel (EXP-608-win011-unnikrishnan-reframe.json:kernel_of_truth). The dome’s offensive use of Unnikrishnan 2001 against the rival globe ‘gravitational shielding’ hypothesis is, narrowly, legitimate, and the prior c10 ‘cites against itself’ framing was screenshot-refutable; correcting it in-text turns the confirmed-reader’s screenshot from a refutation into a corroboration (wins.json:WIN-011/detail_evidence). The abstract-scope quote checks out independently (DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.63.062002).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Being a better argument than the one it replaced does not make the strongest phrasing bulletproof. The defensible core — the paper reads the contact-phase valleys the dome depends on as conventional, not as evidence of new gravity (wins.json:WIN-011/detail_evidence) — fully survives. Only the incremental step ‘rules out the dome’s own mechanism’ over-reaches beyond what Unnikrishnan quantitatively tested (mass-shielding / Majorana coefficient), and that incremental step is the one a dome defender will attack as our own source-stretching (this review, holes_found[0]).

deeper_analysis: The EXP-608 reframe does exactly what it set out to do: it swaps a factually-wrong, screenshot-refutable characterization for a correct and stronger one, and it deflates the ‘silently’ over-repetition. Verdict ‘Not Demonstrated’ remains correct — the dome’s own ‘CONFIRMED (Mechanism Contested)’ label plus a deferred 2026-08-12 SG test makes this a pending wager by the dome’s own scoring. The one residual exposure is symmetric-risk: our review’s central recurring charge against the dome is selective/over-extended use of cited authorities, so the bar for our OWN citations is higher than average. The current text mostly clears it (the ‘treats the valleys as conventional’ clause is airtight) but twice slips into ‘rules out the mechanism,’ which implies a quantitative exclusion of ECM coupling that Unnikrishnan did not perform — they bounded gravitational shielding (Majorana extinction). Recommending a minor_edit to route the claim through ‘rules out the 1997 data as evidence for’ rather than ‘rules out the mechanism.’ No verdict change; no major/critical holes. Note also our local raw-text snapshot is stale (V50.6) and does not contain the live dome’s Unnikrishnan ‘Globe Counter’ block, so the reframe’s factual premise rests on the c10 + EXP-608 fetches rather than the static capture — worth a refresh of 02-wins.txt at some point.
